title: Unop of a limit cone in an opposite category is a colimit cocone
statement: Let $A$ be a small category and $\mathcal C$ a category. The opposite category reverses arrows and composition. Let $D:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a functor, and let $(S,(\pi_a:S\to D(a)))$ be a limit cone: for every object $T$ and compatible family $g_a:T\to D(a)$, there is a unique $v:T\to S$ with $\pi_a\circ v=g_a$ for every $a$. Removing the opposite signs gives a functor $D^{\mathrm{unop}}:A\to\mathcal C$, with objects $D(a)^{\mathrm{unop}}$ and arrows $D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{unop}}$ for $f:a\to b$. Then $(S^{\mathrm{unop}},(\pi_a^{\mathrm{unop}}:D(a)^{\mathrm{unop}}\to S^{\mathrm{unop}}))$ is a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] on $D^{\mathrm{unop}}$. Thus for every cocone $(U,(h_a))$ there is a unique $u:S^{\mathrm{unop}}\to U$ with $u\circ\pi_a^{\mathrm{unop}}=h_a$ for every $a$.
